title: The Search for the Wicked Witch, part 4
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: Forthwith there was heard a great buzzing in the air, and a swarm of black bees came flying toward her.

“Go to the strangers and sting them to death!” commanded the Witch, and the bees turned and flew rapidly until they came to where Dorothy and her friends were walking. But the Woodman had seen them coming, and the Scarecrow had decided what to do.

“Take out my straw and scatter it over the little girl and the dog and the Lion,” he said to the Woodman, “and the bees cannot sting them.” This the Woodman did, and as Dorothy lay close beside the Lion and held Toto in her arms, the straw covered them entirely.

The bees came and found no one but the Woodman to sting, so they flew at him and broke off all their stings against the tin, without hurting the Woodman at all. And as bees cannot live when their stings are broken that was the end of the black bees, and they lay scattered thick about the Woodman, like little heaps of fine coal.
Then Dorothy and the Lion got up, and the girl helped the Tin Woodman put the straw back into the Scarecrow again, until he was as good as ever. So they started upon their journey once more.

The Wicked Witch was so angry when she saw her black bees in little heaps like fine coal that she stamped her foot and tore her hair and gnashed her teeth. And then she called a dozen of her slaves, who were the Winkies, and gave them sharp spears, telling them to go to the strangers and destroy them.

The Winkies were not a brave people, but they had to do as they were told. So they marched away until they came near to Dorothy. Then the Lion gave a great roar and sprang towards them, and the poor Winkies were so frightened that they ran back as fast as they could.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what came buzzing through the air?
options: A swarm of black bees
A flock of wild crows
A cloud of stinging flies
The Winged Monkeys

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what was the Scarecrow's plan against the bees?
options: Scatter his straw over the others to hide them
Have the Woodman cut down a tree for shelter
Send the Lion roaring at the swarm
Have Dorothy cover them with her dress

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happened to the bees that stung the Woodman?
options: They broke their stings on the tin and died
They stung him and flew away again
They were crushed beneath his axe
They turned back to the Witch unharmed

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did the Witch give the Winkies?
options: Sharp spears
Silver whistles
Golden caps
Nothing at all

options: Little heaps of fine coal
Drifts of black snow
Scattered grains of sand
A dark stain on the grass

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why could the bees not hurt anyone?
options: The only one they could reach was made of tin
The Lion's mane was too thick for them
They arrived after the party had gone
Dorothy's white dress frightened them off

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why did the Winkies obey the Witch at all?
options: They were not brave, but had to do as they were told
They hated the strangers as much as she did
They had been promised their freedom for it
They believed the strangers were wizards

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, how were the Winkies driven off?
options: The Lion roared and sprang towards them
The Woodman killed their leader with his axe
The Scarecrow stretched out his arms
Dorothy threw water over them

options: Grinding them together in fury

The Lion alone
The Winkies, out of pity
The Scarecrow himself

options: A dozen
Forty
A hundred
Only two

options: Sting the strangers to death
Drive them back to the city
Steal the girl's silver shoes

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, how did Dorothy and Toto escape the bees?
options: The Scarecrow's straw covered them entirely

They hid in the Woodman's own shadow

options: They cannot live

They return to the hive
